mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1 million units signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < 1000 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes under these conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE > 4.0% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which compresses earnings for industrial firms and drags equity valuations lower, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 5-day returns in more than 70% of triggered INDPRO < -1% months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in the same month signals a sharp labor market deterioration, which reduces consumer demand and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases AND PAYEMS decreases by > 100000 in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not negative in at least 75% of triggered months under these conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average by more than 5% signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces near-term consumption demand and corporate revenues, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average +5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 does not underperform in at least 60% of triggered periods as defined.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both CPIAUCSL (inflation) and FEDFUNDS below 2% for two consecutive months signals an extended period of loose monetary policy in a low-inflation environment, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% AND FEDFUNDS < 2% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a robust manufacturing expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change >= 0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 does not achieve positive 20-day returns in at least 70% of triggered INDPRO expansion periods.
